fullPassage: Stars spend their lives converting hydrogen into helium in their cores to create energy and maintain stability, but their supply of hydrogen is not infinite. In a star, when hydrogen runs short, its core begins to contract, and its outer layers expand. Out of hydrogen, the star fuses heavier elements until it eventually forms iron. Once a star’s core is mostly iron, it can no longer produce energy through fusion and sustain the outward pressure needed to counteract the inward pull of gravity. As a result, it compresses and then explodes, releasing a huge amount of matter into space. If the star’s remaining core is sufficiently massive, scientists believe, it can then collapse under its own gravity and become a black hole, an object whose gravitational pull is so strong that nothing can escape. However, this potential fate is reserved only for the largest stars; smaller stars end their lives as dense remnants that slowly fade away over billions of years.

det.tip: expand(팽창하다) ↔ shrink(줄어들다)

questions.passage: Stars spend their lives converting hydrogen into helium in their cores to create energy and maintain stability, but their supply of hydrogen is not infinite. In a star, when hydrogen runs short, its core begins to contract, and its outer layers expand. Out of hydrogen, the star fuses heavier elements until it eventually forms iron. Once a star’s core is mostly iron, it can no longer produce energy through fusion and sustain the outward pressure needed to counteract the inward pull of gravity. As a result, it compresses and then explodes, releasing a huge amount of matter into space. If the star’s remaining core is sufficiently <u>massive</u>, scientists believe, it can then collapse under its own gravity and become a black hole, an object whose gravitational pull is so strong that nothing can escape. However, this potential fate is reserved only for the largest stars; smaller stars end their lives as dense remnants that slowly fade away over billions of years.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 massive와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
massive(거대한)의 반대는 크기·질량이 매우 작은 tiny(아주 작은)
① enormous(엄청난) — massive와 같은 방향의 유의어
② heavy(무거운) — 질량이 크다는 점에서 오히려 유사
③ distant(멀리 떨어진) — 크기와 무관한 다른 의미축
④ tiny(아주 작은) ✅ 정답 — massive의 반의어
det.tip: massive(거대한) ↔ tiny(아주 작은)

questions.passage:
(A) When the massive star finally explodes, it hurls an enormous amount of <u>matter</u> out into the surrounding space.
(B) Your safety does <u>matter</u> to everyone on this team, so please follow the rules carefully.
questions.stem: 다음 밑줄 친 matter가 (A)의 의미와 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
(A)의 matter는 '물질'을 뜻하는 명사로 쓰였음
① dark matter(암흑 물질) ✅ 정답 — '물질'을 뜻하는 명사로 (A)와 동일
② does not matter(중요하지 않다) ❌ (B)처럼 '중요하다'는 동사
③ something the matter(문제) ❌ '이상, 문제'를 뜻하는 명사
④ as a matter of fact(사실은) ❌ 관용 표현으로 '물질'의 뜻이 아님
det.tip: matter는 명사로 '물질', 동사로 '중요하다', 그 밖에 '문제'나 관용구로도 쓰임

ch: Astronomers estimate how much dark <u>matter</u> exists in the galaxy.
It does not <u>matter</u> to me whether we win or lose today.
There seems to be something the <u>matter</u> with the old engine.
As a <u>matter</u> of fact, the final report was finished yesterday.

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "the natural force that attracts objects toward one another, such as the pull that draws things toward the center of a planet or star"

det.analysis:
'물체를 서로 끌어당기는 자연의 힘'이라는 정의는 gravity(중력)에 해당함
① friction(마찰) — 표면 사이에서 운동을 방해하는 힘, 정의와 다름
② gravity(중력) ✅ 정답 — 정의와 정확히 일치
③ pressure(압력) — 단위 면적에 가해지는 힘을 뜻해 끌어당김과 다름
④ density(밀도) — 단위 부피당 질량을 뜻하는 물리량
det.tip: gravity = 물체를 서로 끌어당기는 힘(중력)

questions.passage: If the star's remaining core is sufficiently massive, scientists believe, it can then collapse under its own gravity and become a black hole, an object whose __________ (gravity) pull is so strong that nothing can escape. However, this potential fate is reserved only for the largest stars.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 빈칸은 명사 pull(당김)을 앞에서 수식하는 형용사 자리이므로, 명사 gravity를 형용사형 gravitational로 바꿔야 함
det.analysis:
빈칸 뒤 명사 pull을 수식하는 형용사가 필요하므로 gravity의 형용사형 gravitational이 정답
명사 gravity를 그대로 두면 명사가 명사를 수식하는 어색한 구조가 되어 문맥상 '중력의 당김'을 나타낼 수 없음
det.tip: 명사 gravity → 형용사 gravitational. 명사를 앞에서 꾸미는 자리인지 확인

questions.passage: Out of hydrogen, the star fuses heavier elements until it __________ (eventual) forms iron. Once a star's core is mostly iron, it can no longer produce energy through fusion and sustain the outward pressure needed to counteract the inward pull of gravity.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 빈칸은 동사 forms를 수식하는 자리이므로, 형용사 eventual을 부사형 eventually로 바꿔야 함
det.analysis:
빈칸 뒤 동사 forms를 수식하는 부사가 필요하므로 형용사 eventual을 부사형 eventually로 바꿔야 함
형용사 eventual을 그대로 두면 동사를 수식할 수 없어 '결국 형성한다'는 의미를 나타낼 수 없음
det.tip: 형용사 eventual → 부사 eventually. 동사를 꾸미는 자리인지 확인

questions.passage: Stars spend their lives converting hydrogen into helium in their cores to create energy and maintain stability, but their supply of hydrogen is not infinite. In a star, when hydrogen __________, its core begins to contract, and its outer layers expand. Out of hydrogen, the star fuses heavier elements until it eventually forms iron. Once a star’s core is mostly iron, it can no longer produce energy through fusion and sustain the outward pressure needed to counteract the inward pull of gravity. As a result, it compresses and then explodes, releasing a huge amount of matter into space. If the star’s remaining core is sufficiently massive, scientists believe, it can then collapse under its own gravity and become a black hole, an object whose gravitational pull is so strong that nothing can escape. However, this potential fate is reserved only for the largest stars; smaller stars end their lives as dense remnants that slowly fade away over billions of years.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
빈칸 뒤에서 '핵이 수축하고 바깥층이 팽창한다'는 별의 노화 과정을 설명하므로, 연료인 수소가 '부족해진다'는 runs short가 적절
① builds up(축적되다) — 수소가 늘어난다는 뜻이라 노화 과정과 반대
② spreads out(퍼지다) — 양의 부족과 무관
③ runs short(부족해지다) ✅ 정답 — 연료 부족으로 별의 변화가 시작됨
④ cools down(식다) — 단순 온도 변화일 뿐 연료 부족을 나타내지 못함
det.tip: when hydrogen ____ → 연료가 '부족해지다'를 뜻하는 runs short

questions.passage: Stars spend their lives converting hydrogen into helium in their cores to create energy and maintain stability, but their supply of hydrogen is not infinite. In a star, when hydrogen runs short, its core begins to contract, and its outer layers expand. Out of hydrogen, the star fuses heavier elements until it eventually forms iron. Once a star’s core is mostly iron, it can no longer produce energy through fusion and sustain the outward pressure needed to counteract the inward pull of gravity. As a result, it compresses and then explodes, releasing a huge amount of matter into space. If the star’s remaining core is sufficiently massive, scientists believe, it can then collapse under its own gravity and become a black hole, an object whose gravitational pull is so strong that __________. However, this potential fate is reserved only for the largest stars; smaller stars end their lives as dense remnants that slowly fade away over billions of years.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: nothing can escape=아무것도 빠져나갈 수 없다
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞에서 '중력이 너무 강해서(so strong that)'라고 했으므로, 그 결과로 아무것도 빠져나가지 못한다는 nothing can escape가 적절
① objects can enter freely(물체가 자유롭게 들어간다) — 빠져나감이 아닌 유입이라 초점이 어긋남
② light easily passes through(빛이 쉽게 통과한다) — 강한 중력으로 빛조차 못 빠져나간다는 사실과 반대
③ new planets can form(새 행성이 생긴다) — 블랙홀의 특성과 무관
④ nothing can escape(아무것도 빠져나갈 수 없다) ✅ 정답 — 강한 중력의 결과
det.tip: gravitational pull is so strong that ____ → 아무것도 빠져나갈 수 없다는 블랙홀의 핵심 특성
